questions.title: The night shift
questions.alt: A volunteer yawning beside boxes of donated food.
questions.clues: Leo worked all night and has not slept. He is yawning.

why.must: The lack of sleep and his yawning strongly support this deduction. Here, must means almost sure, not an obligation.
why.might: This sentence is possible, but might expresses uncertainty. The task asks for a strong deduction.
why.can’t: This means you are almost sure he is not tired. The clues point in the opposite direction.

questions.title: The empty backpack
questions.alt: Two students check an empty backpack with open pockets.
questions.clues: Nora has emptied her backpack and checked every pocket twice. Nothing is left inside, but her keys are still missing.
questions.sentence: The keys ___ be in the backpack.

why.must: Must be in the backpack conflicts with the evidence: the bag and all its pockets are empty.
why.might: Might leaves the bag as a possible location. The task asks you to rule it out using the completed search.
why.can’t: The bag and every pocket have been checked and are empty. The clues let us rule out that location.

questions.model: The keys can’t be in the backpack.

questions.title: A call from London
questions.alt: A classroom laptop shows a friend on a video call from London.
questions.clues: You are in a classroom in Medellín. Your friend Emma is speaking to you on a live video call from London right now.
questions.sentence: Emma ___ be in your classroom now.

why.must: Must be in your classroom conflicts with the clue that she is in London right now.
why.might: Might would leave the classroom as a possible location. The live call from London rules that out in this situation.
why.can’t: She is in London at this moment, so you can rule out her being in your classroom in Medellín at the same time.

questions.model: Emma can’t be in your classroom now.

questions.title: The result is in
questions.alt: A student smiles with relaxed shoulders after a presentation.
questions.clues: Mia was afraid she had failed her presentation. She has just learned that she passed. Now she smiles and her shoulders relax.

why.must: The good result and her change in expression strongly suggest relief. We are making a deduction from several clues.
why.might: Might is possible English, but it is less certain. The instruction asks for a strong deduction.
why.can’t: Can’t be relieved means almost sure she is not relieved. Her reaction and the good news support the opposite.

questions.title: Before the presentation
questions.alt: A student holds note cards before speaking to classmates.
questions.clues: Ana is holding her notes tightly before speaking. You have not asked how she feels. She could be nervous, or she could simply be concentrating.

why.must: Holding notes tightly does not prove nervousness. The situation gives another possible explanation.
why.might: Nervousness is a possible explanation, but we are not sure. Might leaves room for another explanation.
why.can’t: The clues do not rule out nervousness. Can’t would express much stronger certainty that she is not nervous.

questions.title: During the talk
questions.alt: A learner rests his cheek on his hand during a talk.
questions.clues: Ben rests his cheek on his hand during a talk. You do not know whether he is bored, tired or thinking carefully.

why.must: His posture alone is not enough for this strong conclusion. He could also be tired or thinking.
why.might: Boredom is one possible explanation. The other possibilities mean we should not sound certain.
why.can’t: Nothing here rules out boredom. Can’t would express certainty that he is not bored.

questions.title: A wet arrival
questions.alt: A volunteer arrives with a wet jacket and a dripping umbrella.
questions.clues: Luis has just come in from outside. His jacket is wet, water is dripping from his umbrella, and you hear heavy rain on the roof.

why.must: The wet jacket, dripping umbrella and sound on the roof give strong evidence of rain.
why.might: Might expresses a possibility, but the task asks for a strong deduction supported by several clues.
why.can’t: Can’t be raining means almost sure it is not raining. That conflicts with the clues.

questions.title: A locked library
questions.alt: Two students check a locked library entrance with a dark interior.
questions.clues: It is 9 p.m. The library closes at 6 p.m. today. The entrance is locked, the lights are off, and no special event is scheduled.
questions.sentence: The library ___ be open to visitors now.

why.must: Must be open means you are almost sure it is open. The closing time, locked door and dark interior support the opposite.
why.might: Might be open leaves this possibility open. The task asks for a strong negative deduction from the clues.
why.can’t: The closing time, locked door and dark interior strongly suggest it is not open to visitors now. This is a deduction, not a rule.

questions.model: The library can’t be open to visitors now.

questions.title: At the bus stop
questions.alt: A woman checks her watch at a bus stop.
questions.clues: Sara is looking at her watch at a bus stop. You do not know her plans. Perhaps she is meeting a friend, or perhaps she is waiting for a bus.
questions.sentence: She ___ be waiting for a friend.

why.must: Checking a watch does not tell us who she is waiting for. Must would express more certainty than these clues support.
why.might: Meeting a friend is one possible explanation. We do not have enough information to be sure.
why.can’t: Nothing rules out meeting a friend. Can’t would express a strong negative deduction.

questions.model: She might be waiting for a friend.

questions.title: At the museum
questions.alt: Museum visitors lean forward and watch a guide demonstrate a model.
questions.clues: The visitors lean forward, ask many questions and ask the guide to continue. They have stayed much longer than planned.
questions.sentence: They ___ be interested in the exhibition.

why.must: Their attention, questions and wish to stay longer strongly support interest. Must expresses this strong deduction.
why.might: Might expresses only a possibility. The task asks for the stronger deduction supported by several clues.
why.can’t: Can’t be interested means almost sure they are not interested. Their actions strongly suggest the opposite.

questions.model: They must be interested in the exhibition.
